## What cost time or turns

- **Steps 24 and 50: tunnel drops read as agent failures.** At 20 calls at a time, tool calls went through the free ngrok tunnel without a result; the mock log showed no request for that minute. About 20 cases in run-18 and 5 in run-19 failed this way, and the judge wrote "technical errors". It took one look at the mock log's per-minute counts (step 33) to see it. At 12 calls at a time (run-20) it did not happen. Cost: most of run-19 (2m52s) re-tested infrastructure.

## Lessons for any brief

- A tool call with no result, plus no matching request in the hosted mock's log, means the tunnel dropped it under load. Re-run those cases; do not fix the agent for them.
- A leftover generator for the same brief is a good starting point even when the registry is empty.
- Pass the brief's own API file to `--check` as well as to the benchmark.

- `A generator left by an earlier session of the same brief is the starting point even when the agent registry is empty: review it against the brief, regenerate with the current base URL and save; that put the first full run at minute 1.`

- `Restart a hosted mock whenever its file may have changed, and before judging a fault case, check the mock log that the fault fired. # Builder lessons

What the practice runs taught, kept outside `.claude/` so that the builder can write here: Claude Code refuses edits to the skill files in the builder's permission mode, and lessons left in a retrospective never reached the next run.

Both skills read this file at their first step. The retrospective (test-phone-agent, section "Retrospective") updates it: one line per lesson, general only — no rule, number, date, name, product, queue, outcome value or holiday from any brief — at most 12 lines per section; merge, replace or drop old lines rather than growing the list.

## Building the agent

- Check which tool API file matches the brief: `tools/openapi.json` is the collections API of Briefs A and B. When the brief has its own tool table or a per-brief API file, use that, and pass the tool base URL to the generator as a parameter instead of writing it into the workflow by hand.
- Write the workflow from a generator script; compile every hook and exec it locally on sample inputs before the first save. Never patch code strings through shell heredocs: escaped newlines come out as real ones.
- In post-hooks, read request fields that a pre-hook stored in `vars`; do not rely on `<tool>_args` being set yet.
- Before writing the workflow, POST once to the bank host for every tool the brief names; a "not found" means the practice mock cannot play that tool — record it and plan the tests around it.
- A 404 "not found" for the stored workflow or agent is not transient: back up `.freya-agents.json`, drop that slot's entry, and save again to re-create it.
- If `python3` is not found, run the same command with `python`.
- Speak the closing summary from a fixed line computed in code and run the close as an engine call after it, on every exit path including transfers: the model often calls a closing tool without its closing sentence.
- A rule that counts failed answers must count every reply to the question in code; the model does not forward non-answers ("I don't have it") to a validation tool.
- Set any "a write was attempted" flag in the write's pre-hook and clear it in the post-hook on success: a post-hook does not see an error or timeout response, so state written only there is missing exactly when the timed-out-write path needs it.
- A request that must escalate from any point of the call (a security report mid-collection) belongs in a global `matches_intent` node with an engine-run transfer; a system-prompt rule alone lost to the current step's own offer.
- Never point a model-facing helper (a "wrap up", "check field" or "next step" tool) at a real bank endpoint: every call lands in the bank's ledger, trips the cases' forbidden tools and reads to the judge as a needless call. Let the model end a step through an extracted variable and a route instead, and keep tool calls for what the bank must record or answer.

## Testing and fixing

- Before the first run, clear leftovers: `python3 tools/benchmark.py` tells you when the workspace is busy with another simulation and recreates a persona cache another workspace left behind; old mocks and tunnels on your port must go by hand (take the URL from your own tunnel's log).
- Never pipe a benchmark through `tail` or `head`: run it with `python -u`, in the foreground, and read its output; "waiting for the workspace" then shows at once instead of after the timeout.
- A 5xx while a simulation is being polled does not stop it on Freya; the runner keeps polling now. If a command was still cut off, or a full run stopped at its time limit, the simulation may still hold the workspace for minutes: the next run queues behind it.
- Restart a hosted mock whenever its file may have changed, and before judging a fault case, check the mock log that the fault fired; a fault that never fires tests nothing and the judge then fails the agent on side remarks.
- Smoke-test with `--only` on one case per exit path (create, transfer, status, close) before the first full run, and start that run by minute 6: a full run of 60+ cases took 13 to 16 minutes (the calls at a time adapt to the share of slow replies; at 5 and at 8 calls a sixth of the replies took over 10 seconds, so the shared model's own load mattered more than ours), so the budget holds one first full run, one or two `--only` fix rounds and one last full run.
- A wrong security answer in a case must be unrelated to the fixture's value; a swapped or transposed variant can trigger a hint that the brief does not count as wrong.
- In case scripts, have the persona give the decisive fact or action in its first relevant answer, before anything that could move the call into another branch.
- When the brief prescribes wording for a reply, put that phrase verbatim in the prompt or a fixed line; the judge rejects paraphrases. Word each check with the same sentence boundaries as the brief's rule, and never forbid a word the brief makes the agent say.
- A rule about what happens after a write cannot be reached if the call ends at the write; test it at the read-back instead.
- After a fix, re-run the failed cases plus a neighbour from the same family with `--only`, then keep about 8 minutes for a final full run.
- When every customer hangs up after its first sentence and the agent said nothing, the shared model was down (once for 24 minutes), not the agent: the judge still writes "the customer ended the call", which reads like an agent fault. Probe with `--probe`, change nothing until it answers.

I built the Brief F agent, tested it in four benchmark runs, and did the retrospective. The last full run passed 61 of 63 cases, but that was version 3; the final version 4 has only had a 3-case re-run, because a 10-minute full run would not fit in the 30 minutes.

**Build.** No agent was registered for Brief F, but an earlier session had left a workflow generator for this brief. I reused it rather than starting from scratch, so the first full run started about a minute in. Instead of fresh web research on the banking terms, I relied on the brief and that generator.

**Runs:**

| Run | Version | What | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | full set, 20 calls at a time | 40 / 63 |
| 2 | 2 | re-run of the 23 failures | 16 / 23 |
| 3 | 3 | full set, 12 calls at a time | 61 / 63 (all 13 universal cases passed) |
| 4 | 4 | re-run of 3 cases | 2 / 3 |

**Why the first runs scored low.** Most of those failures were not the agent's fault. At 20 calls at a time, the agent's tool calls never reached the practice mock bank behind the free ngrok tunnel, and the mock's log shows no request for those calls. At 12 calls at a time, in run 3, it did not happen.

**Agent fixes, all made in the prompts:**
- **Third parties:** the agent was offering the security questions to someone calling for their partner. It now says it can only deal with the account holder, and explains that the questions protect the account.
- **Read-back:** it once asked "Shall I submit this application?" without reading the values back. It also submitted a second application of the same type after the first had gone through.
- **Digits in pieces:** a postcode given in parts was counted as wrong answers and ended in a transfer. That case now passes.

**Still open:**
- **GEN-48 fails:** the talkative test customer never gives the phone digits, so this is a problem with the case script. It also shows that when that step runs out of turns, the call closes with the wrong reason ("out of scope").
- **Failed-answer count:** the count before a transfer offer (rule 13) still depends on the prompt, not on code.
- **Hidden-brief estimate:** version 3 scored 58 of 60, with low confidence. Version 4 has no estimate because only 3 cases ran on it.
- **Placeholder address:** before submitting, regenerate `out/brief-f.workflow.json` with the real tool address. It currently holds a placeholder (`https://SUBMISSION-BASE-URL/v1`) so the tunnel address isn't left in the file.

I stopped the mock and the tunnel. The retrospective is in `reports/brief-f-retro.md` and the run review in `results/bench/brief-f/run-20.review.md`. I added one new lesson to `docs/builder-lessons.md` and extended two existing lines:
- **New:** reuse a generator left for the same brief.
- **Extended:** pass the brief's own tool definition file to the case check as well as to the benchmark.
- **Extended:** tool calls that leave no trace in the mock's log were dropped by the tunnel, so re-run those cases instead of changing the agent.

- **Digits in pieces:** a postcode given in parts was counted as wrong answers and ended in a transfer. That case now passes.

**Still open:**
- **GEN-48 fails:** the talkative test customer never gives the phone digits, so this is a problem with the case script. It also shows that when that step runs out of turns, the call closes with the wrong reason ("out of scope").
- **Failed-answer count:** the count before a transfer offer (rule 13) still depends on the prompt, not on code.
- **Hidden-brief estimate:** version 3 scored 58 of 60, with low confidence. Version 4 has no estimate because only 3 cases ran on it.
- **Placeholder address:** before submitting, regenerate `out/brief-f.workflow.json` with the real tool address. It currently holds a placeholder (`https://SUBMISSION-BASE-URL/v1`) so the tunnel address isn't left in the file.

I stopped the mock and the tunnel. The retrospective is in `reports/brief-f-retro.md` and the run review in `results/bench/brief-f/run-20.review.md`. I added one new lesson to `docs/builder-lessons.md` and extended two existing lines:
